Include a declaration of use
A declaration must be included in your assignment after your reference list. It should detail which
tools you have used to generate content in the process of completing your assignment and how
they have been employed. The declaration must include the prompts you have used to generate
information.

We further recommend that all students and staff acknowledge when and how they have used
GenAI, particularly in any work that will be assessed, published, or shared with others.

If you use a Generative AI (Gen-AI) tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude,
or Copilot, when completing an assessment, it is recommended to
declare your use. Additionally, if you have used Gen-AI to create
content that you include in your work, you must reference this use
as a source of information.

A glossary of definitions is also provided as a quick reference guide. This guide should be read in
conjunction with Statute No. 10 – Student Discipline and Student Misconduct Rules, and should not
be used as a replacement.

D3.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Compatible rules, without explicit coordination): N133 and N136 require a GenAI declaration ('must') specifically when GenAI is approved for content generation in an assessment, whereas N134 (university-wide guidance across assessment, research, and shared work) and A005 (general Library referencing advice) frame general acknowledgement as 'recommended' while requiring referencing if GenAI-created content is included. Because these provisions address different scopes/circumstances, they are compatible rather than contradictory. Minor uncoordinated points remain: N136 p.151 marks Gemini pre-submission feedback with a green tick without restating the p.149 Unit Coordinator permission condition, and N002 p.44 still cross-references the superseded Academic Misconduct Rules rather than Student Misconduct Rules 2026 (N141).
